head.prepared_by: Tax team — drafted with Korean Tax MCP (law 0.15.3, calculator 0.53.1)
head.re: Korean withholding tax on a patent royalty paid by a Korean subsidiary to its US parent
head.scope: Illustrative facts (hypothetical company); Korean tax only, US tax not covered

summary.conclusion: Withhold KRW 16,500,000 on a KRW 100,000,000 royalty.
summary.basis: That is KRW 15,000,000 of corporate tax at the 15 percent treaty cap plus KRW 1,500,000 of local corporate income tax.[^t14][^local]

summary.conclusion: Without the treaty application on file before payment, withhold KRW 22,000,000.
summary.basis: The domestic rate is 20 percent plus local tax. The treaty rate needs a reduced-rate application and proof of beneficial ownership from the US parent, and from 2026 the payer must also file the application with the tax office.[^cta98][^cta98_6][^cta98_6_4]

summary.conclusion: An unregistered patent no longer means zero tax.
summary.basis: The Supreme Court's en banc decision of 18 September 2025 treats the royalty as Korean-source whenever the patented technology is in fact used in Korea, whether or not the patent is registered here.[^sc2021]

question: How much Korean tax must a Korean subsidiary withhold when it pays a KRW 100,000,000 patent and technology royalty to its US parent corporation in 2026, and what does the Korea–US tax treaty change?

short_answer.conditions: The payment is a royalty under the treaty; the technology is used in Korea; the US parent is the beneficial owner and files the reduced-rate application before payment; the royalty is not connected with a Korean permanent establishment of the parent; and the amount is arm's length. If the contract is net of Korean tax, the tax base is grossed up and the tax is higher.

facts: Payer: a Korean corporation (subsidiary). Recipient: its US parent, a US corporation and US tax resident.

facts.text: Payment: KRW 100,000,000 for the use of patents and technology, paid in 2026. The amount is gross: the parent bears the Korean tax.
The subsidiary uses the patented technology in manufacturing and sales in Korea.
The US parent is the beneficial owner of the royalty and has no permanent establishment in Korea connected with it.
The reduced-rate application is received by the subsidiary before the payment date.
The royalty is within the arm's-length range.

analysis.heading: The payment is a royalty — if it is for the use of patents or existing know-how
analysis.rule: The treaty defines royalties as payments of any kind for the use of, or the right to use, patents, designs, secret processes or know-how.[^t14] A fixed price for the outright transfer of a patent is not a royalty.[^sc2022]
analysis.application: On the facts given, the subsidiary pays for the use of the parent's patents and technology. The contract has not been reviewed, so it is not known whether it bundles services, software or a transfer.
analysis.conclusion: Treated as a royalty. The rule is verified; the classification depends on the contract.
analysis.confirm: Contract deliverables (licence, know-how transfer, engineers, training, software), the confidentiality clause, and how the fee is computed.

analysis.heading: Korea may tax it — the technology is used in Korea, registered here or not
analysis.rule: Royalties are Korean-source where the right or information is used in Korea, including a patent not registered in Korea whose technology is in fact used here.[^cta93] The treaty sources royalties where the property is used,[^t6] and the Supreme Court held in 2025 that "use" means use of the patented technology.[^sc2021]
analysis.application: The subsidiary is assumed to manufacture and sell in Korea using the technology. Whether the patents are registered in Korea therefore does not change the result.
analysis.conclusion: Korean-source royalty. A "not registered, so 0 percent" position is no longer available for 2026 payments. Verified. No Supreme Court decision on the statutory wording in force since 2020 was found (not verified).
analysis.confirm: Patent list and countries of registration, licensed territory, whether the fee is based on Korean or worldwide sales, and evidence for any use outside Korea.

analysis.heading: Domestic law sets the rate at 20 percent of the amount paid
analysis.rule: Korean-source royalty income paid to a foreign corporation is subject to withholding at 20 percent of the amount paid, at the time of payment.[^cta98]
analysis.application: The payment is KRW 100,000,000 gross, so the domestic withholding would be KRW 20,000,000 of corporate tax.
analysis.conclusion: 20 percent applies unless the treaty rate is properly claimed. Verified.

analysis.heading: A net-of-tax contract grosses up the tax base
analysis.rule: Where the contract provides for payment net of Korean taxes, the tax base is the agreed amount divided by one minus the withholding rate.[^grossup]
analysis.application: If KRW 100,000,000 were the net amount and the subsidiary bore the corporate tax at the 15 percent treaty rate, the base would be KRW 117,647,058 and the corporate tax KRW 17,647,058.
analysis.conclusion: This memo assumes a gross contract. The formula is verified; including local income tax in the rate is inferred.
analysis.confirm: The tax clause in the contract and whether the invoice amount is gross or net.

analysis.heading: The treaty caps the corporate tax at 15 percent for a patent royalty
analysis.rule: Korean tax on royalties derived by a US resident may not exceed 15 percent of the gross amount; a 10 percent cap applies only to copyright royalties for literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works and to film royalties.[^t14] The cap does not apply to a royalty connected with a Korean permanent establishment or to the excess over an arm's-length amount.[^t14_35]
analysis.application: A patent and technology royalty falls under the 15 percent cap, not the 10 percent cap. No permanent establishment and an arm's-length amount are assumed.
analysis.conclusion: 15 percent: KRW 15,000,000 of corporate tax. Verified.

analysis.heading: The 15 percent rate needs an application before payment — and a filing by the payer from 2026
analysis.rule: The beneficial owner must give the payer a reduced-rate application and proof of beneficial ownership before payment; without them the payer withholds at the domestic rate.[^cta98_6] For applications made from 2026, the payer must file the application with its tax office by the end of February of the following year; a correction claim is possible within five years.[^cta98_6_4]
analysis.application: The memo assumes the application is received before the payment date. As a 2026 application, it must be filed by the subsidiary by the end of February 2027.
analysis.conclusion: The treaty rate is available only with the paperwork. Verified. Whether a US residency certificate must be attached was not verified.
analysis.confirm: Date the application was received against the first payment date; who files it with the tax office.

analysis.heading: Local income tax is added on top — 10 percent of the corporate tax
analysis.rule: The treaty covers the Korean income tax and corporation tax only, so the treaty rate is the corporate tax portion; 10 percent of the corporate tax withheld is collected separately as local corporate income tax.[^local]
analysis.conclusion: Total withholding is KRW 16,500,000, or 16.5 percent of the royalty. Verified.

rows: Technology used only outside Korea, proved by the taxpayer
Copyright royalty for literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works, or film
Patent or know-how royalty, application on file before payment
No application, or beneficial owner not confirmed

scenarios.title: Net-of-tax contract (subsidiary bears the corporate tax)

calculation.note: Amounts for the first two tables are from the calculator (nonresident_withholding: 2026, corporation, United States). The rounding unit for the net-of-tax case was not verified.

risks.why: No application or beneficial-owner proof before payment means 20 percent, not 15. A parent that must pass the royalty on to another group company may not be the beneficial owner.[^cta98_6]
risks.check: The application, proof of beneficial ownership, any conduit in the chain, and the filing with the tax office by the end of February 2027.[^cta98_6_4]

risks.why: If the subsidiary bears the Korean tax, the base is grossed up and KRW 16,500,000 understates the tax.[^grossup]
risks.check: The tax clause and whether local income tax is also borne by the subsidiary.

risks.point: Use in Korea and unregistered patents
risks.why: Since the 2025 en banc decision, registration in Korea no longer decides the source. Only the part proved to be used outside Korea is excluded, and the Tax Tribunal puts that proof on the taxpayer (조심 2025중2984, 13 April 2026).[^sc2021]
risks.check: Licensed territory, fee base, and records separating use in and outside Korea.

risks.why: Pure services performed in the United States are not Korean-source, and a fixed price for a patent transfer is not a royalty; mixed contracts follow the main part or are apportioned (inferred for the service case).[^sc2022]
risks.check: Deliverables, where services are performed, and other fees paid to the parent.

risks.why: The excess over an arm's-length royalty falls outside the 15 percent cap and may be adjusted and treated as a dividend to the parent.[^t14_35][^ictca]
risks.check: Royalty rate, benchmark licences, and whether the KRW 100 million threshold for the statement of international transactions is exceeded.

risks.why: No VAT reverse charge arises if the royalty is used wholly in a taxable business (Value-Added Tax Act (부가가치세법), Art. 52(1)); a royalty tied to imported goods may be added to customs value (Customs Act (관세법), Art. 30(1)(4)). Customs cases were not reviewed.
risks.check: Any VAT-exempt business of the subsidiary and imports from the parent group.

next_steps.action: Obtain the reduced-rate application and proof of beneficial ownership from the US parent.
Review the licence agreement: deliverables, tax clause (gross or net), licensed territory and fee base.
Withhold KRW 16,500,000 at payment, remit it by the 10th of the following month and give the parent the withholding receipt.
File the reduced-rate application with the tax office and the payment statement.

footnotes.text: Korea–United States Income Tax Convention (signed 15 June 1976, in force 20 October 1979), Art. 14(1): tax on royalties “shall not exceed 15 percent of the gross amount”; Art. 14(2): 10 percent for copyright royalties for literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works and for film royalties; Art. 14(4)(a): royalties include payments for patents and know-how. Verified.

Convention, Art. 1 (taxes covered: for Korea, the income tax and the corporation tax); Corporate Tax Act (법인세법), Art. 98-7(1)(1); Local Tax Act (지방세법), Art. 103-52(1): 10 percent of the corporate tax withheld is collected as local corporate income tax. Verified.
Corporate Tax Act, Art. 98(1)(6): 20 percent of the amount paid on Korean-source royalty income under Art. 93(8), withheld at payment and remitted by the 10th of the following month. Verified.

Corporate Tax Act, Art. 98-6(1) and (3) (법인세법 제98조의6); Enforcement Decree, Art. 138-7(1): the beneficial owner files the reduced-rate application and proof of beneficial ownership with the payer before payment; otherwise the payer withholds at the Art. 98(1) rate. Verified.
Corporate Tax Act, Art. 98-6(4) (added 23 December 2025; Addenda No. 21217, Art. 13: applications made on or after 1 January 2026) and Art. 98-6(5) (correction claim within five years). Verified.

Supreme Court (대법원), en banc decision of 18 September 2025, 2021두59908: royalties for a patent not registered in Korea are Korean-source where the patented technology is used in Korea; earlier decisions to the contrary (e.g. 27 November 2014, 2012두18356) overruled. Followed in Supreme Court, 11 December 2025, 2022두30744. Verified (full text read).
Supreme Court, 9 April 2026, 2022두66002: Art. 14(4)(b) of the Convention covers only contingent consideration; a fixed price for the transfer of a patent is not a royalty. Verified.
Corporate Tax Act, Art. 93(8), including item (c) on patents not registered in Korea (applies to income paid on or after 1 January 2020; Addenda No. 16833, Art. 8). Verified.
Convention, Art. 6(3): royalties are treated as income from sources within a Contracting State only if paid for the use of the property in that State. Verified.

Corporate Tax Act Basic Rules (법인세법 기본통칙) 98-0…2: tax base = agreed amount ÷ (1 − withholding rate). Verified. Local income tax counts among the “taxes under Korean tax law” according to the summary of NTS ruling 국이22601-403 (19 July 1991); the formula in that ruling was not verified.
Convention, Art. 14(3) (royalty effectively connected with a permanent establishment) and Art. 14(5) (amount exceeding what would have been paid to an unrelated person). Verified.
Adjustment of International Taxes Act (국제조세조정에 관한 법률), Art. 7(1), Art. 13(1) and Art. 16. Verified. How the earlier royalty withholding is settled against a dividend adjustment was not verified.

prepared_how: Statutes (as of 31 December 2026), treaty articles, court decisions and rulings were retrieved with korean-tax-mcp 0.15.3 (law_article, tax_treaty, treaty_withholding_rates, search_tax_rulings) and the amounts with korean-tax-calc-mcp 0.53.1 (nonresident_withholding) on 15 November 2026, then written up in English. Each conclusion is labelled verified (source text read), inferred, or not verified. Korean statute text governs; English renderings of article names are for convenience.
